legend: This classic small intestinal example is lined by zones of site-specific mucosa and lamina propria partitioned by cords of smoth muscle.
A Peutz–Jeghers polyps most frequently involve the small intestine and consist of normal mucosal components organized in lobules by arborizing smooth muscle bundles.
B The smooth muscle bundles divide the polyp into discrete lobules and do not entrap epithelium like a mucosal prolapse-type polyp.

Mucosal prolapse polyps also contain a significant component of smooth muscle. However, the smooth muscle branching is more haphazard and often wraps around individual colonic crypts. These polyps are common in the rectosigmoid region and should not be diagnosed as sporadic Peutz–Jeghers polyps.

Large polyps of any type with prolapse may show fibromuscular proliferation in the lamina propria. The syndromic juvenile polyp shown here in a patient with germline BMPR1A mutation also shows branching smooth muscle fibres, which should not be mistaken for a Peutz–Jeghers polyp.
